evals.name: design-only-local-conventions
evals.prompt: We're adding an incident dashboard to Northstar for support leads monitoring active incidents and handoffs. Use the supplied DESIGN_SYSTEM.md as our existing product conventions. Propose a visual direction before we build it. It needs a scannable incident list, severity, an owner, and a next-update time; it must also work on phones. This is a design brief only, not a request to write code.
evals.expected_output: A design-only proposal with two or three distinct viable directions, trade-offs, a recommendation and memorable differentiator, while preserving the supplied local design system and mobile/accessibility constraints.
assertions: Presents two or three viable design directions with explicit trade-offs and recommends one.
Names a concrete memorable differentiator while covering incident severity, owner, and next-update time.
Preserves system-ui typography and flat, undecorated surfaces from the local design system.
Explains phone-width behavior and accessible status communication without returning implementation code.

evals.name: apply-approved-direction
evals.prompt: Update the supplied EmailSettings.tsx for production use. Its visual direction is already approved; follow DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, keep the current Props API, and don't propose a redesign. Users need to edit their email and save it reliably on desktop or mobile, including when onSave is slow or rejects. Return the complete replacement component in a TSX code block and a short verification note; do not modify files for this exercise.
evals.expected_output: A complete replacement React component using native form semantics, associated labels, pending/success/error handling, no duplicate submits, responsive layout, and local tokens, without reopening the approved design direction or claiming unrun tests passed.
assertions: Returns a complete replacement EmailSettings component preserving the email/onSave Props API, without proposing alternative design directions.
Uses a native form, an associated email label, and a native submit button for keyboard operation.
Awaits onSave, prevents duplicate pending submissions, and provides pending, success, and recoverable error feedback.
Replaces fixed-width overflow with a fluid layout and uses local design tokens without decorative additions.
Distinguishes source inspection from unrun runtime, browser, or accessibility checks.

evals.name: review-only-concrete-findings
evals.prompt: Review the supplied EmailSettings.tsx against our DESIGN_SYSTEM.md. Focus on keyboard access, form reliability, and phone-width behavior. Give me actionable findings only, with source locations; don't implement the fixes or redesign the page.
evals.expected_output: A read-only, findings-first report with file:line locations and bug/regression risk/polish classifications, identifying the non-keyboard save control, missing label association, missing async states/error handling, and fixed-width mobile overflow. Note testing gaps without claiming browser verification.
assertions: Returns findings first with EmailSettings.tsx line references and bug, regression risk, or polish classifications; does not return replacement code.
Identifies the click-only div save control as a keyboard-access problem and recommends native form/button semantics.
Identifies the missing programmatic label association and explains a concrete correction.
Identifies unhandled async save failure and lack of pending protection or feedback with actionable corrections.
Identifies the 640px fixed-width mobile overflow and notes that runtime/browser verification was not performed.
